brief: Europe is cracking under surging gas, rising yields, French sovereign stress and yen strength, with the OAT/Bund spread breaking to new highs and spilling into equity vol. The index has broken its 50-day, with next support at 6,200 and the 200-day near 6,000. US tech has not broken. AI demand keeps strengthening: Google Cloud's $100m-plus deals are growing over 2x quarter over quarter and year over year, AI-server payback is under two years, and Broadcom's demand exceeds its $115bn FY27 outlook, with power, site readiness and supply now the constraint, not demand. Tech CDS spreads have widened since mid-August without the NDX sell-off that accompanied July's spike. The second-order risk is a yen-funded carry unwind draining US leverage as capital returns to Japan, and USDJPY vol has surged ahead of VIX. Six-month SPX realized correlation has fallen to 11, a level seen only before February 2007 and January 2018's Volmageddon, historically followed by an explosive return of vol convexity, while SPX straddles sit near yearly lows. Convexity is judged cheap, so owning the eventual break (long SPX straddles, or BofA's sell the October 16 VIX put, buy the November 22-30 call spread) is preferred over guessing its direction.
